Applied to its earnings per share of ₹1.36 in Q1FY27 (₹5.44 for a full year), a share would be worth ₹224.04 (low), ₹258.49 (middle) or ₹302.69 (high).
Against the top of the price band, ₹271, the middle value means 4.6% downside.
Q1FY27 covers only part of a year; scaling it up assumes the rest of the year goes the same way.
The EV/EBITDA cross-check couldn't be done: Needs total borrowings and cash for the same date, to go from company value to the owners' share.
This is a rough guide, not a forecast: it assumes the company deserves the same price tag as its listed peers.
